summary: Hermann Bonitz worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1830–1834) and Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg (~1834–1836). He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry (~1875–1888).

Hermann Brockhaus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel and Christian Lassen (~1829–1834). He served as professor at the University of Jena (1839–1841) and the University of Leipzig (1841–1877).

Hermann Brunnhofer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bonn, Berlin under Albrecht Weber (~1868–1870), and Zurich. He held positions at Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek (1873–1888), Saint Petersburg State University (1891–1901), and the University of Bern as Dozent (1901–1914).

Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (1859–1862), studying under Hermann Brockhaus and Georg Curtius in 1859. He was a teacher at Thomasschule zu Leipzig (~1864–1904) and Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau (1887).

Hermann Collitz worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Göttingen under August Fick, Berlin, and Halle. He held academic posts at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928), and served as president of the Linguistic Society of America (1924–1925).

Hermann Diels worked in philosophy, history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1866–1867) and the University of Bonn under Hermann Usener (~1867–1870). From ~1882 to 1922, he held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin.
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He subsequently served as a professor at the University of Giessen from ~1893 to 1922.

Hermann Ethé worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Greifswald, Leipzig (Ph.D. 1863–1865), Munich, and Oxford. He catalogued Oriental manuscripts at the Bodleian Library (1872) and was Professor of Oriental Languages at Aberystwyth University from 1875.

Hermann Friedrich Mögling was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1829–1834) and the Basel Mission Seminary (1834). From 1838 to 1852, he served as a teacher and preacher for the Basel Mission.

Hermann Fränkel studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff (~1906–1910), University of Bonn, and University of Göttingen. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1920–1935) and Stanford University (~1935–1953).

Hermann Goetz was an Indologist and art historian who earned his Ph.D. at Munich and studied under Jean Philippe Vogel. He held curatorial posts at the Baroda Museum (1939–1953) and National Gallery of Modern Art, later directing art history at Heidelberg (1961–1976).

Hermann Grassmann worked in Indology, linguistics, and other fields. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher and August Boeckh (1827–1830). He later taught mathematics at several schools and served as a professor at Marienstiftsgymnasium (~1852–1877).

Hermann Gundert was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen (~1831–1835). He was associated with the Church Missionary Society (~1836–1838) and the Basel Mission (1838), and served as head of Calwer Verlag starting in 1860.

Hermann Güntert worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies, studying at Heidelberg under Hermann Osthoff and Christian Bartholomae. He became ord. Professor at the University of Rostock (1921) before serving as ordinary Professor of IE linguistics at Heidelberg University (1926–1945).

Hermann Hirt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg and Leipzig under Brugmann, Leskien, Zarncke, Sievers, and Windisch. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig (1891–1912) and ordinary professor at the University of Giessen (1912–1936).

Hermann Hunger is an archaeologist and linguist who studied at Vienna, Münster, and Heidelberg. He held positions at the German Archaeological Institute (~1970–1973), the University of Chicago (~1973–1978), and served as a professor at the University of Vienna (1978–2007).

Hermann Hupfeld worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1813–1817) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1819–1822). He held academic posts at Marburg (~1825–1843) and Halle-Wittenberg (~1843–1866).

Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Berlin and Bonn under Johann Gildemeister. He served as professor at the University of Münster (1876–1885) and the University of Bonn (Privatdozent 1875, Professor 1889–1922).

Hermann Kopp worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Leipzig, the Walleser-Institut, and Heidelberg under Max Walleser and Heinrich Zimmer. He directed the Walleser-Institut (1954–1958), Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz (1959–1964), and Heidelberg University (1964).

Hermann Kreyenborg was an Indologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Münster, where he completed his Ph.D. under Richard Schmidt (~1919–1921). He served as a librarian at the University and State Library of Münster (1922–1954).
